opportunities.title: [Bounty: $100] URL-encode path parameters in client `get`/`update` methods
opportunities.summary: ## Context `AgentClient.get(agentId)` and `update` build `path: /v1/agents/${agentId}` (`src/clients/agent-client.ts`, lines 22-24 and 37-40); `WalletClient.get` does the same with `${walletId}` (`src/clients/wallet-client.ts`, lines 18-22); `PaymentClient.get` with `${paymentId}` (`src/clients/payment-client.ts`, lines 27-31). The transport builds the URL with `new URL(cleanPath, baseUrl)` (`src/http/fetch-http-client.ts`, line 106) but never percent-encodes the interpolated segment. Any id containing `/`, `?`, `#`, or a space silently corrupts the request URL and can hit the wrong route. ## Proposed Change Add a small `encodePathSegment`/`encodeURIComponent` step in `BaseClient.request` (or in `buildUrl`) so interpolated path parameters are always percent-encoded before the URL is constructed. ## Acceptance Criteria - A `get` call with an id containing `/` or `?` hits the correctly encoded path - `BaseClient` is the single place that handles path encoding for all clients - Encoding is applied in `agent`, `wallet`, and `payment` clients - Regression tests cover special-character ids for each client ## Suggested Label bug

opportunities.title: [Bounty: $95] Retry timed-out requests when retry budget remains
opportunities.summary: ## Context In the request loop in `src/http/fetch-http-client.ts`, an aborted fetch is immediately thrown as `LilyTransportError` with code `TIMEOUT` (lines 77-82); timeouts never reach the `isRetryableTransportError` path (lines 84-88). A server that is merely slow on the first attempt consumes the whole retry budget, even though a second attempt would likely succeed — inconsistent with how the transport treats other transient failures on idempotent methods. ## Proposed Change Treat `AbortError` as a retryable transport error for idempotent methods (GET/PUT/DELETE) when `attempt < config.retry.retries`, keeping the timeout check inside the same guard as other transport errors. Document that non-idempotent requests still fail fast on timeout. ## Acceptance Criteria - A GET that times out once is retried when `retries > 0` - A GET that times out on every attempt throws `LilyTransportError` with code `TIMEOUT` - POST timeouts are never retried - A test asserts the retry and exhaustion paths ## Suggested Label bug

opportunities.title: [Bounty: $95] Deep-freeze the resolved retry policy in `ResolvedLilySdkConfig`
opportunities.summary: ## Context `resolveLilySdkConfig` freezes `defaultHeaders` (`src/config/resolve-config.ts`, lines 37-39) but returns the retry policy and its `retryableStatusCodes` array as mutable plain objects, and `ResolvedLilySdkConfig` (`src/config/types.ts`, lines 14-23) is marked `readonly` only at the top level. Because `config` is public on `LilySdk` (`src/sdk.ts`, line 12), consumers can mutate `sdk.config.retry.retryableStatusCodes` at runtime and silently alter transport behavior. ## Proposed Change Deep-freeze the resolved `retry` object (including the `retryableStatusCodes` array), matching the existing `defaultHeaders` treatment. Add a test asserting mutation attempts are no-ops. ## Acceptance Criteria - `Object.isFrozen(sdk.config.retry)` is true - `Object.isFrozen(sdk.config.retry.retryableStatusCodes)` is true - `defaultHeaders` continues to be frozen - A test asserts frozen-ness of the resolved config ## Suggested Label refactor

opportunities.title: [Bounty: $90] Only set `content-type: application/json` when a request has a body
opportunities.summary: ## Context `buildHeaders` in `src/http/fetch-http-client.ts` (lines 117-138) always sets `content-type: application/json`, including for `GET`/`DELETE` requests that carry no body (e.g., `AgentClient.list`, `SystemClient.health`, `WalletClient.get`). Some HTTP servers and edge proxies reject or log warnings for requests that declare a JSON content type with no body, and it misrepresents the request. A missing body on a `POST`/`PATCH` is already handled (lines 32-34 only assign `body` when defined), so the header should mirror that. ## Proposed Change Only set `content-type` when `serializeBody(request.body)` returns a value, and keep the unconditional `accept: application/json`. ## Acceptance Criteria - GET requests carry no `content-type` header - POST/PATCH requests with a body still set `content-type: application/json` - Existing tests that assert headers continue to pass after updating expectations - A test asserts both cases ## Suggested Label bug

opportunities.title: [Bounty: $80] Raise a clear error for 200 responses with empty JSON bodies
opportunities.summary: ## Context `parseResponse` in `src/http/fetch-http-client.ts` (lines 148-160) calls `response.json()` whenever the `content-type` is `application/json`. When the server returns 200 with an empty body (common for some backends), `response.json()` throws a raw `SyntaxError`. In the request loop that error falls into the `catch` (line 70), is not an `AbortError` or `LilyApiError`, and for GET/PUT/DELETE it is silently retried and finally surfaced as `LilyTransportError` with code `TRANSPORT_ERROR` (lines 84-93) — a misleading diagnosis for what is really a payload mismatch. ## Proposed Change Catch empty-body JSON parse failures inside `parseResponse` and return `null` (mirroring the 204 path), or wrap the failure in a `LilyValidationError` with a message naming the status and content-type so callers can distinguish it from a network failure. ## Acceptance Criteria - A 200 with `content-type: application/json` and an empty body no longer throws `SyntaxError` - The failure is surfaced as a typed error, not a `TRANSPORT_ERROR` retry - A regression test covers the empty-JSON-body case ## Suggested Label bug
